plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Endless ribbons of violet-blue spikes ripple across sun-baked hillsides, releasing a warm, herbal perfume that hums with bees. Each slender stem carries whorls of tiny tubular blossoms above silvery-green foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with peak bloom in July
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Dinner-plate-sized blossoms rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. Pink-tipped petals open at dawn and fold shut by evening, and they release a sweet, fruity fragrance over still ponds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, with flowering from July to August
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across temperate East Asia, including Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic waxy texture that makes water bead up and roll away, carrying dirt with it. Scientists call this the 'lotus effect' and have copied it in self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: In the cool of the Australian winter, this shrub lifts glowing, bottlebrush-like spikes of orange to burnt-gold flowers. They light up sandstone heathlands and draw honeyeaters and other nectar-feeding birds.
plants.location: Coastal eastern Australia, especially the Sydney region of New South Wales
plants.funFact: A single flower spike packs in thousands of tiny individual flowers. After flowering, the spikes develop woody cones that hold their seeds until fire opens them.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: South Africa's national flower is a spectacular crown of pointed pink bracts around a downy, creamy heart. It is the largest bloom in the protea family and brings drama to the winter fynbos.
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient lineage that dates back tens of millions of years. The family is named after the Greek sea god Proteus, who could change his shape.
